cards.front: How do MHC class I and MHC class II differ?
cards.back: **MHC I** (HLA-A, -B, -C): on all nucleated cells; has **β2-microglobulin**; shows **cytosolic** peptides (loaded in the ER via **TAP**) to **CD8+** T cells. **MHC II** (HLA-DP, -DQ, -DR): on **antigen-presenting cells**; shows **endocytosed** peptides to **CD4+** T cells.
cards.back_pt: **MHC I** (HLA-A, -B, -C): em todas as células nucleadas; tem **β2-microglobulina**; apresenta peptídeos **citosólicos** (carregados no RE via **TAP**) aos linfócitos T **CD8+**. **MHC II** (HLA-DP, -DQ, -DR): em **células apresentadoras de antígeno**; apresenta peptídeos **endocitados** aos linfócitos T **CD4+**.

cards.front: What happens in positive and negative selection of T cells in the thymus?
cards.back: **Positive selection** (cortex): thymocytes that bind self-MHC weakly survive (**MHC restriction**). **Negative selection** (medulla): thymocytes that bind self-antigen strongly die. **AIRE** lets medullary epithelial cells show tissue antigens; AIRE loss causes autoimmunity (**APS-1**).
cards.back_pt: **Seleção positiva** (córtex): timócitos que se ligam fracamente ao MHC próprio sobrevivem (**restrição ao MHC**). **Seleção negativa** (medula): timócitos que se ligam fortemente a antígenos próprios morrem. O **AIRE** faz as células epiteliais medulares exibirem antígenos de tecidos; a perda do AIRE causa autoimunidade (**SPA-1**, síndrome poliglandular autoimune tipo 1).

cards.front: What do Th1, Th2 and Th17 cells secrete, and what is each one for?
cards.back: **Th1** (induced by IL-12): **IFN-γ** activates macrophages against intracellular microbes. **Th2** (induced by IL-4): **IL-4, IL-5, IL-13**; IgE, eosinophils, helminths. **Th17** (induced by TGF-β plus IL-6; kept active by IL-23): **IL-17** recruits neutrophils against extracellular bacteria and fungi.
cards.back_pt: **Th1** (induzido por IL-12): **IFN-γ** ativa macrófagos contra micro-organismos intracelulares. **Th2** (induzido por IL-4): **IL-4, IL-5, IL-13**; IgE, eosinófilos, helmintos. **Th17** (induzido por TGF-β mais IL-6; mantido ativo pela IL-23): **IL-17** recruta neutrófilos contra bactérias extracelulares e fungos.

cards.front: Which markers identify regulatory T cells, and how do they suppress immune responses?
cards.back: Tregs are **CD4+ CD25+** (CD25 is the IL-2 receptor α chain) and express the transcription factor **FOXP3**. They release **IL-10** and **TGF-β** and suppress self-reactive T cells. Loss-of-function FOXP3 mutation causes **IPEX** syndrome.
cards.back_pt: As Treg são **CD4+ CD25+** (CD25 é a cadeia α do receptor de IL-2) e expressam o fator de transcrição **FOXP3**. Liberam **IL-10** e **TGF-β** e suprimem linfócitos T autorreativos. Mutação com perda de função do FOXP3 causa a síndrome **IPEX**.

cards.front: What two signals does a naive T cell need for activation, and what blocks it?
cards.back: **Signal 1**: the TCR (signaling through **CD3**) binds peptide-MHC. **Signal 2**: **CD28** on the T cell binds **B7 (CD80/86)** on the APC. Signal 1 alone causes **anergy**. **CTLA-4** (takes B7 away from CD28) and **PD-1** (binds PD-L1) are inhibitory.
cards.back_pt: **Sinal 1**: o TCR (que sinaliza via **CD3**) liga-se ao peptídeo-MHC. **Sinal 2**: o **CD28** do linfócito T liga-se ao **B7 (CD80/86)** da APC. O sinal 1 sozinho causa **anergia**. **CTLA-4** (retira o B7 do CD28) e **PD-1** (liga-se ao PD-L1) são inibitórios.

cards.front: How do CD8+ cytotoxic T cells kill an infected cell?
cards.back: They recognize a foreign peptide on **MHC I**, then release **perforin**, which makes pores in the target membrane, and **granzymes**, which enter and activate **caspases**, causing **apoptosis**. They can also use **Fas ligand** to bind Fas on the target.
cards.back_pt: Reconhecem um peptídeo estranho no **MHC I** e liberam **perforina**, que forma poros na membrana da célula-alvo, e **granzimas**, que entram e ativam **caspases**, causando **apoptose**. Também podem usar o **ligante de Fas** para se ligar ao Fas da célula-alvo.

cards.front: How do B cells generate and then improve antibody diversity?
cards.back: **V(D)J recombination** by **RAG1/RAG2** in the bone marrow builds the variable region before any antigen contact. After antigen contact, **AID** drives **somatic hypermutation** (→ **affinity maturation** in germinal centers) and **class switching**, which needs **CD40–CD40L** plus cytokines.
cards.back_pt: A **recombinação V(D)J** pelas **RAG1/RAG2** na medula óssea monta a região variável antes de qualquer contato com antígeno. Após o contato com antígeno, a **AID** promove **hipermutação somática** (→ **maturação da afinidade** nos centros germinativos) e **troca de classe**, que exige **CD40–CD40L** mais citocinas.

cards.front: What is the key role of each immunoglobulin class?
cards.back: **IgM**: made first; pentamer; strong complement activator. **IgG**: most abundant; crosses the **placenta**; opsonizes. **IgA**: dimer in secretions and breast milk (**secretory component**). **IgE**: binds mast cells and basophils; allergy, helminths. **IgD**: on naive B cells.
cards.back_pt: **IgM**: produzida primeiro; pentâmero; forte ativadora do complemento. **IgG**: a mais abundante; atravessa a **placenta**; opsoniza. **IgA**: dímero nas secreções e no leite materno (**componente secretor**). **IgE**: liga-se a mastócitos e basófilos; alergia, helmintos. **IgD**: em linfócitos B virgens.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old boy has had repeated sinus and ear infections since age 6 months. He is now admitted with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Serum IgM is high, while IgG, IgA and IgE are very low. Flow cytometry shows normal numbers of B cells and T cells. A lymph node biopsy shows no germinal centers. Failure of which interaction best explains his findings?
choices: CD28 on T cells with B7 on antigen-presenting cells
CD40 ligand on helper T cells with CD40 on B cells
T-cell receptor with peptide on MHC class II
Fas ligand with Fas on target cells
IL-2 with the IL-2 receptor α chain (CD25) on T cells
questions.explanation: B cells make IgM first; switching to IgG, IgA or IgE needs **CD40 ligand** on activated CD4+ T cells to bind **CD40** on B cells. Without it there is no **class switching** and no germinal centers, so IgM is high and the other classes are low. CD40L also helps T cells activate macrophages, which explains the *Pneumocystis* infection. A CD28-B7 defect would block T-cell activation broadly and would not give this isolated isotype pattern (the immunodeficiency block covers hyper-IgM syndromes).
questions.explanation_pt: Os linfócitos B produzem IgM primeiro; a troca para IgG, IgA ou IgE exige que o **ligante de CD40** dos linfócitos T CD4+ ativados se ligue ao **CD40** dos linfócitos B. Sem isso não há **troca de classe** nem centros germinativos, então a IgM fica alta e as outras classes ficam baixas. O CD40L também ajuda os linfócitos T a ativar macrófagos, o que explica a infecção por *Pneumocystis*. Um defeito CD28-B7 bloquearia a ativação de linfócitos T de forma ampla e não daria esse padrão isolado de isotipos (as síndromes de hiper-IgM estão no bloco de imunodeficiências).

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man has 2 weeks of fatigue, dark urine and jaundice. Serum ALT is 1,450 U/L. HBsAg and IgM anti-HBc are positive. A liver biopsy shows scattered shrunken, eosinophilic hepatocytes with condensed nuclei, next to lymphocytes. Immunostaining shows that most of these lymphocytes are CD8+. Which mechanism most directly kills the infected hepatocytes?
choices: Membrane attack complex formed after antibody binding
Hydrogen peroxide released by neutrophils
Direct cytopathic damage from viral replication
Granzymes entering through perforin pores and activating caspases
Histamine released by degranulating mast cells
questions.explanation: In acute hepatitis B, **CD8+ cytotoxic T cells** recognize viral peptides on **MHC I** of hepatocytes. They release **perforin** and **granzymes**; granzymes activate **caspases** and the cells die by **apoptosis** (the shrunken eosinophilic hepatocytes). Direct viral damage is the tempting answer, but hepatitis B virus is not directly cytopathic: the liver injury comes mainly from the immune response.
questions.explanation_pt: Na hepatite B aguda, os **linfócitos T citotóxicos CD8+** reconhecem peptídeos virais no **MHC I** dos hepatócitos. Eles liberam **perforina** e **granzimas**; as granzimas ativam **caspases** e as células morrem por **apoptose** (os hepatócitos retraídos e eosinofílicos). O dano viral direto é a resposta tentadora, mas o vírus da hepatite B não é diretamente citopático: a lesão hepática vem principalmente da resposta imune.

questions.stem: A 26-year-old man returns from a year of volunteer work in rural Southeast Asia, where he often walked barefoot. He has had 3 weeks of mild abdominal discomfort. Leukocyte count is 11,500/mm3 with 22% eosinophils. Serum IgE is high. Stool microscopy shows Strongyloides stercoralis larvae. A CD4+ T-cell response is driving his blood findings. Which cytokine most directly increases his eosinophil count?
choices: Interleukin-2
Interleukin-4
Interferon-gamma
Interleukin-17
Interleukin-5
questions.explanation: Helminths trigger a **Th2** response. Th2 cells release **IL-5**, which drives the production, activation and survival of **eosinophils**. IL-4 is the tempting answer: it promotes Th2 differentiation and B-cell class switching to **IgE** (the high IgE here), but it is not the main eosinophil growth factor. IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-17 (Th17) direct responses against intracellular microbes and extracellular bacteria or fungi.
questions.explanation_pt: Os helmintos desencadeiam uma resposta **Th2**. As células Th2 liberam **IL-5**, que estimula a produção, a ativação e a sobrevida dos **eosinófilos**. A IL-4 é a resposta tentadora: ela promove a diferenciação Th2 e a troca de classe dos linfócitos B para **IgE** (a IgE alta aqui), mas não é o principal fator de crescimento dos eosinófilos. O IFN-γ (Th1) e a IL-17 (Th17) direcionam respostas contra micro-organismos intracelulares e contra bactérias extracelulares ou fungos.

questions.stem: A 4-month-old girl is exclusively breastfed and healthy. Her mother asks how breast milk protects the baby's gut. The main antibody in breast milk is made by plasma cells in the mammary gland as a dimer joined by a J chain. It is then carried across the glandular epithelium into the milk. Which feature most helps this antibody resist digestive enzymes in the infant's gut?
choices: Secretory component derived from the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor
Pentameric structure that binds many antigens at once
Binding to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)
High-affinity binding to the Fc epsilon receptor on mast cells
Strong activation of the classical complement pathway
questions.explanation: This is **secretory IgA**. Dimeric IgA binds the **polymeric immunoglobulin receptor** on the basolateral side of epithelial cells and is carried to the lumen. Part of the receptor stays attached as the **secretory component**, which protects IgA from proteases. FcRn is the tempting answer because it protects antibody from breakdown, but it binds only **IgG**: it carries IgG across the placenta and extends its half-life, and does not act on IgA. The pentamer describes IgM.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **IgA secretora**. A IgA dimérica liga-se ao **receptor de imunoglobulina polimérica** na face basolateral das células epiteliais e é transportada até o lúmen. Parte do receptor fica ligada como **componente secretor**, que protege a IgA das proteases. O FcRn é a resposta tentadora porque protege anticorpos da degradação, mas ele só se liga à **IgG**: transporta a IgG pela placenta e prolonga sua meia-vida, sem agir sobre a IgA. O pentâmero descreve a IgM.

notes.title: Adaptive immunity: MHC, T cells, B cells and antibodies
notes.body_md:
## MHC and antigen presentation

- **MHC I** (HLA-A, -B, -C): all nucleated cells; cytosolic peptides; recognized by **CD8+** T cells.
- **MHC II** (HLA-DP, -DQ, -DR): antigen-presenting cells; endocytosed peptides; recognized by **CD4+** T cells.
- HLA disease associations are covered with each disease.

## T-cell development and activation

- Thymic cortex: **positive selection** (MHC restriction). Medulla: **negative selection** of strongly self-reactive cells, helped by **AIRE**.
- Activation needs **signal 1** (TCR-CD3 with peptide-MHC) and **signal 2** (**CD28-B7**). Signal 1 alone causes **anergy**.
- **CTLA-4** and **PD-1** turn T cells off.
- **IL-2** drives T-cell proliferation.

## T-cell effector types

- **Th1**: IFN-γ; macrophages, intracellular microbes.
- **Th2**: IL-4, IL-5, IL-13; IgE, eosinophils, helminths.
- **Th17**: IL-17; neutrophils, extracellular bacteria and fungi.
- **Tfh**: IL-21 and CD40L; help B cells in germinal centers.
- **Treg**: CD25, FOXP3; IL-10 and TGF-β.
- **CD8+** cells kill with **perforin and granzymes** or Fas ligand.

## B cells and antibodies

- **V(D)J recombination** (RAG1/RAG2) happens before antigen contact.
- **AID** drives **somatic hypermutation** (affinity maturation) and **class switching**.
- Switching needs **CD40-CD40L** plus cytokines: **IL-4** → IgE, **TGF-β** → IgA.
- IgM first and pentameric; IgG crosses the placenta; secretory IgA protects mucosa; IgE binds mast cells.

## Primary vs secondary response

- **Primary**: slower, lower, mainly **IgM**.
- **Secondary**: memory cells give a faster, larger, high-affinity **IgG** response.

## Tolerance

- **Central**: deletion in the thymus and bone marrow.
- **Peripheral**: anergy, Tregs, inhibitory receptors.

## Related blocks

- Lymph node and spleen structure: hematopoiesis block.
- Immunodeficiency diseases: their own block.
- Hypersensitivity and transplant rejection: their own block.
- Vaccines and passive antibodies: immunopharmacology block.
notes.body_pt_md:
## MHC e apresentação de antígenos

- **MHC I** (HLA-A, -B, -C): todas as células nucleadas; peptídeos citosólicos; reconhecido por linfócitos T **CD8+**.
- **MHC II** (HLA-DP, -DQ, -DR): células apresentadoras de antígeno; peptídeos endocitados; reconhecido por linfócitos T **CD4+**.
- As associações de HLA com doenças estão em cada doença.

## Desenvolvimento e ativação dos linfócitos T

- Córtex do timo: **seleção positiva** (restrição ao MHC). Medula: **seleção negativa** das células fortemente autorreativas, com ajuda do **AIRE**.
- A ativação exige o **sinal 1** (TCR-CD3 com peptídeo-MHC) e o **sinal 2** (**CD28-B7**). O sinal 1 sozinho causa **anergia**.
- **CTLA-4** e **PD-1** desligam os linfócitos T.
- A **IL-2** estimula a proliferação dos linfócitos T.

## Tipos efetores de linfócitos T

- **Th1**: IFN-γ; macrófagos, micro-organismos intracelulares.
- **Th2**: IL-4, IL-5, IL-13; IgE, eosinófilos, helmintos.
- **Th17**: IL-17; neutrófilos, bactérias extracelulares e fungos.
- **Tfh**: IL-21 e CD40L; ajudam os linfócitos B nos centros germinativos.
- **Treg**: CD25, FOXP3; IL-10 e TGF-β.
- Os linfócitos **CD8+** matam com **perforina e granzimas** ou com ligante de Fas.

## Linfócitos B e anticorpos

- A **recombinação V(D)J** (RAG1/RAG2) ocorre antes do contato com o antígeno.
- A **AID** promove **hipermutação somática** (maturação da afinidade) e **troca de classe**.
- A troca exige **CD40-CD40L** mais citocinas: **IL-4** → IgE, **TGF-β** → IgA.
- IgM é a primeira e é pentamérica; IgG atravessa a placenta; IgA secretora protege a mucosa; IgE liga-se a mastócitos.

## Resposta primária vs secundária

- **Primária**: mais lenta, menor, principalmente **IgM**.
- **Secundária**: células de memória geram resposta de **IgG** mais rápida, maior e de alta afinidade.

## Tolerância

- **Central**: deleção no timo e na medula óssea.
- **Periférica**: anergia, Treg, receptores inibitórios.

## Blocos relacionados

- Estrutura do linfonodo e do baço: bloco de hematopoese.
- Doenças por imunodeficiência: bloco próprio.
- Hipersensibilidade e rejeição de transplantes: bloco próprio.
- Vacinas e anticorpos passivos: bloco de imunofarmacologia.
